acquisition method: Liquid chromatography–tandem mass spectrometry measurements of prepared samples were performed using a QExactive HF-X mass spectrometer (ThermoFisher Scientific, Palo Alto, CA, USA) operating in data-dependent acquisition mode, coupled with nanoLC.
alkylation reagent: Cysteine alkylation was performed by the incubation of samples in darkness at room temperature for 20 min with 100 µL of 55 mM iodoacetamide solution in the UA buffer followed by centrifugation at 10,000 g for 15 min at room temperature.
alkylation concentration: Cysteine alkylation was performed by the incubation of samples in darkness at room temperature for 20 min with 100 µL of 55 mM iodoacetamide solution in the UA buffer followed by centrifugation at 10,000 g for 15 min at room temperature.
cleavage agent: First, proteins were digested overnight with LysC at 1:50 enzyme to protein ratio in the digestion buffer... samples were subjected to digestion by trypsin overnight at 1:100 enzyme to protein ratio in the digestion buffer... samples were digested by chymotrypsin for three hours at 1:100 enzyme to protein ratio in 10 mM CaCl2 in 100 mM Tris-HCl pH 7.8.
collision energy: fragmented by HCD with normalized collision energies of 25
enrichment method: EVs were isolated from the blood serum using the Total Exosome Isolation (from serum) reagent (Invitrogen) according to the manufacturer’s procedure (Figure 1a).
fragmentation method: fragmented by HCD with normalized collision energies of 25
instrument: Liquid chromatography–tandem mass spectrometry measurements of prepared samples were performed using a QExactive HF-X mass spectrometer (ThermoFisher Scientific, Palo Alto, CA, USA) operating in data-dependent acquisition mode, coupled with nanoLC.
labeling: We compared two methods of label-free protein quantification: Total Protein Approach and MaxQuant LFQ.
reduction reagent: A 1% SDS buffer (100 mM Tris-HCl pH 8, 50 mM DTT, 1% SDS) was used at the ratio of 1:5 (EVs: buffer) for 10 min at 95 °C to lyse obtained EVs and reduce disulfide bonds of released proteins.
reduction concentration: A 1% SDS buffer (100 mM Tris-HCl pH 8, 50 mM DTT, 1% SDS) was used at the ratio of 1:5 (EVs: buffer) for 10 min at 95 °C to lyse obtained EVs and reduce disulfide bonds of released proteins.
